questions.question: ______,also known as search unemployment, occurs when workers lose their current job and are in the process of finding another one.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Frictional unemployment. **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Frictional unemployment** is a type of unemployment that occurs when workers **move from one job to another job.**
 
• It is sometimes called **search unemployment** and can be based on the circumstances of the individual.
 
• **Frictional unemployment is time spent between jobs when a worker is searching for a job or transitioning from one job to another.**​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seasonal unemployment **occurs when people are unemployed at particular times of the year when demand for labor is lower than usual.
 
• **Technological unemployment** occurs when developments in technology and working practices cause some workers to lose their jobs. Technological unemployment is considered to be part of a wider concept known as structural unemployment.
 
• **Cyclical unemployment** is the component of overall unemployment that results **directly from cycles of economic upturn and downturn. Cyclical unemployment** is the impact of economic recession or expansion on the total unemployment rate.

questions.question: Which among the following lakes is known as the only "Floating Islands Lake" in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Loktak Lake__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Loktak Lake is the largest freshwater lake in North-eastern region of the country.
 
• It is famous for Phumdis.
 
• It is located in Manipur.
 
• Keibul Lamjao is the only floating national park in the world floats over it.
 
• Area: 266 square kilometre.
 
• Two wetlands of India are in Montreux Record: Keoladeo National Park(Rajasthan) and Loktak Lake(Manipur).
 
• Montreux Record is also maintained as part of the Ramsar List.
 
• It is under the Ramsar Convention is a register of wetland sites on the List of Wetlands of International Importance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__Chilika Lake__

__
 
• Chilika is Asia’s largest and world’s second-largest lagoon.
 
• It spreads over Puri, Khurda and Ganjam districts of Odisha on the east coast of India, at the mouth of the Daya River.
 
• It is the largest wintering ground for migratory birds on the Indian subcontinent.
 
• In 1981, it was designated the first Indian wetland of international importance under the Ramsar Convention.
 
• Nalbana Bird Sanctuary or Nalbana Island is the core area of the Chilika Lake.

Sambhar Lake__

__
 
• Sambhar Salt Lake, an ephemeral salt lake, the largest lake in India, is situated in east-central Rajasthan state, west of Jaipur.
 
• It represents a depression of the Aravalli Range with 230 square km in area.
 
• It is also known as the salt lake of Rajasthan. 

Pangong Lake__

__
 
• Pangong Tso Lake located in Ladakh__ Union territory is an endorheic lake in the Himalayas situated at a height of about 4,350 m.
 
• It is geographically situated in a disputed territory, claimed both by India and China.
 
• This lake is about 5 km wide and about 134 km long with about 60% of the length extending into Tibet.
 
• Pangong Lake in Kashmir is the world's highest brackish lake at 4,350 m above sea level.

questions.question: Which famous sportsperson has received the Bharat Ratna award in 2014?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Sachin Tendulkar__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 2014, Sachin Tendulkar became the first and the only sportsperson to be conferred with the Bharat Ratna. 
 
• Sachin Tendulkar debuted in 1989.
 
• He played 664 international cricket matches in a career spanning over two decades.
 
• He holds various cricket records including the only player to have scored one hundred international centuries, the first batsman to score a double century in a One Day International, and the only player to complete more than 34,000 runs in both ODI and Test cricket.
 
• Calls have been made over the years to award Major Dhyan Chand with Bharat Ratna, the country’s highest civilian award. But never happened.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award of the Republic of India.
 
• The Bharat Ratna was introduced on 2 January 1954.
 
• It is awarded in recognition of exceptional service/performance of the highest order in any field of human endeavor. 
 
• The number of annual awards is restricted to a maximum of three in a particular year. 
 
• On conferment of the award, the recipient receives a Sanad (certificate) signed by the President and a medallion.
 
• The first recipients of the Bharat Ratna who were honored in 1954 are as follows:
 
 
• C. Rajagopalachari - The last Governor-General of the Dominion of India 
 
• Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan - Second President and the First Vice President of India
 
• C. V. Raman - Nobel Prize Laureate, Physicist

questions.question: What is the atomic mass of sodium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**23**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The atomic mass of an element represents the average mass of an atom of that element, taking into account the different isotopes and their relative abundances.
 
• Sodium is a chemical element with the symbol Na and atomic number 11. It belongs to the alkali metal group on the periodic table.
 
• The atomic mass of sodium is approximately 22.99 atomic mass units (AMU).
 
• The atomic mass of an element is calculated by summing the masses of its isotopes, multiplied by their respective abundances, and expressed in atomic mass units.
 
• Sodium has two stable isotopes: sodium-23 (Na-23) and sodium-22 (Na-22).
 
• The most abundant isotope of sodium is sodium-23, which accounts for approximately 100% of natural sodium. It has an atomic mass of 22.98976928 amu.
 
• Sodium-22 is a less abundant isotope and has an atomic mass of 21.994437 amu.
 
• The atomic mass listed on the periodic table for sodium (22.99 amu) is a weighted average of the masses of its isotopes, considering their natural abundance.
 
• The atomic mass of an element may be slightly different from the mass number of its most abundant isotope due to the presence of other isotopes and their relative abundances.
 
• The atomic mass of sodium is important in various scientific fields, such as chemistry and physics, as it is used in stoichiometric calculations, determining molar mass, and understanding the behavior of sodium in chemical reactions.

questions.question: Humayun's Tomb situated in Delhi is built by_____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Biga Begum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Humayun's Tomb:

 
 
• The tomb of Humayun is located in Delhi.
 
• 
 
Humayun died in 1556, and his widow B**iga Begum​,** **also known as Haji Begam**, commenced the construction of his tomb in 1569, fourteen years after his death. It is the first distinct example of proper Mughal style, which was inspired by Persian architecture. It is well known that Humayun picked up the principles of Persian architecture during his exile, and he himself is likely to have planned the tomb, although there is no record to that effect. The tomb was constructed at a cost of 15 lakh rupees (1.5 million).

 
 
• 
 
Mirak Mirza Ghiyath, a Persian, was the architect employed by Haji Begam for this tomb.

 
 
• It was also the first structure of its size to use red sandstone.
 
• In 1993, the tomb was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bc104fb08a2830deaf8ca0bdc871f921974ab3c9730a92edcc28653115830d7a.png]

• In the Battle of Chausa, in 1539 and Battle of Bilgram, in 1540 (Battle of Kanauj), Humayun was defeated by Sher Khan.
 
• After losing his kingdom, Humayun became an exile for the next 15 years.
 
• In 1555, Humayun defeated the Afghans and recovered the Mughal Throne.
 
• He died in 1556 due to his fall from the staircase of his library.
 
• He loved painting and wrote poetry in the Persian language.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Living organisms can survive a wide range of pH change.
When pH of rain water is less than 8.2, it is called acid rain.
Our body works within the pH range of 7.0 to 7.8.
Tooth decay starts when the pH of the mouth is lower than 1.5.

questions.solution:

• **pH**

 
 
• pH means the potential of Hydrogen.
 
• The pH scale is the scale used to express the acidity or alkalinity of a substance based on the concentration of hydrogen ions in its solution.
 
• pH scale was discovered by Soren Sorensen.
 
• The range of pH scale 0 to 14.
 
 
• If pH 7 then solution is basic.
 
• If pH = 7 then solution is neutral
 
 
 
• The strength of acids and bases depends on the number of H+ ions and OH- ions produced, respectively.
 
• When the pH of rainwater is less than 5.6, it is called acid rain.
 
• The pH value of the Milk of Magnesia is 10.5.

questions.question: _________is the change in total utility due to consumption of one additional unit of a commodity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Marginal utility (MU)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Marginal utility__ - 

 __
 
• It is the additional utility derived from the consumption of an additional unit of a commodity.
 
• Marginal utility is also known as **Marginal Satiety**.
 
• MU = **Change in TU/Change in Quantity**
 
• MU= **TUn - TU****n-1** 
 
• Also, Marginal Utility is the additional utility made to be TU by the additional consumption of one more unit of a commodity.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Product Utility (PU)**

 
 
• ​Product Utility (PU) refers to the perceived value or usefulness that a product provides to its** users or customers**.
 
• It is a concept commonly used in marketing and product development to assess and understand the benefits and satisfaction** derived from a product**
 
 
 
• **Revenue Utility (RU)**
 
 
• Revenue Utility (RU) refers to the economic benefit or value that a consumer derives from purchasing and consuming a particular** good or service**.
 
• It is a concept used in economics to measure the satisfaction or utility that individuals receive from the money they **spend on goods and services**.
 
 
 
• **Demand utility (DU)**
 
 
• Demand utility (DU) refers to the satisfaction or value that an individual or consumer derives from consuming or using a** particular good or service**.
 
• It is a concept commonly used in economics and consumer theory to measure the subjective benefit or enjoyment a consumer obtains from** a product**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Liver Fluke - 

 
 
• The scientific name of liver fluke is Fasciola hepatica.
 
• The life history of liver fluke involves two hosts (Digenetic parasitic).
 
• Primary host - Sheep and goat
 
• Secondary host - Garden snail (Planorbis, Lymnea)
 
• Liver fluke belongs to the **phylum Platyhelminthes, not Nematoda.**
 
• Liver fluke is a parasitic flatworm that infects the liver of its primary host, which is usually a sheep or goat.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sycon - Porifera**

 
 
• Sycon is a sponge that belongs to the phylum Porifera.
 
• The common name of the Sycon is Crown Sponge.
 
• All sponges have a canal system that consists of the Ostia, spongocoel, and osculum.
 
• Canal system is one of the most important features of sponges.
 
• The canal system is a network of canals that connect the spongocoel to the outside via ostia.
 
• It helps in nutrition, respiration, and excretion processes.
 
 
 
• **Prawns - Arthropoda**
 
 
• Prawn is a common name for small aquatic crustaceans with an exoskeleton and ten legs (i.e.** a member of the order decapoda**), some of which can be eaten. 
 
• They belong to the kingdom Animalia and order **Arthropoda**.
 
 
 
• **​Starfish - Echinodermata**
 
 
• Starfish belongs to the phylum Echinodermata group.
 
• Echinodermata are so named owing to their spiny skin (from the Greek “echinos” meaning “spiny” and “dermos” meaning “skin”).
 
• Echinodermata are exclusively marine organisms. Sea stars, sea cucumbers, sea urchins, sand dollars, and brittle stars are all examples of echinoderms.

questions.question: Kalinga is the ancient name of coastal______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Kalinga is the ancient name of a region in eastern India that corresponds to the present-day states of **Odisha and parts of northern Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• It was a significant coastal region known for its **rich cultural heritage and maritime trade.**
 
• The history of Kalinga dates back to ancient times, with references to the region found in texts such as the **Mahabharata and the Puranas**.
 
• **Kalinga **was renowned for its seafaring abilities and flourishing trade connections with other parts of India and foreign lands.
 
• The region was known for its maritime trade in goods like **textiles, spices, precious stones, and other commodities.**
 
• **Kalinga** also had a rich political history. It was ruled by several dynasties and was often engaged in power struggles with neighboring kingdoms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• One of the most notable events in the history of Kalinga was the** Kalinga War **in** 261 BCE.**
 
• This war was fought between the **Mauryan Empire, led by Emperor Ashoka, and the Kalinga Kingdom.**
 
• The war had a significant impact on **Emperor Ashoka, **who was deeply affected by the destruction and loss of life, leading him to embrace Buddhism and renounce violence.
 
• Over time, the name Kalinga fell out of use, and the region came to be known by different names during various historical periods.
 
• The present-day state of Odisha, which encompasses a significant portion of the ancient Kalinga, has a diverse cultural heritage and is known for its art, architecture, dance, and festivals. The coastal areas of Odisha have beautiful beaches and are popular tourist destinations.

questions.question: The Arctic Ocean is located within the Arctic Circle and surrounds the North Pole. It is connected with the Pacific Ocean by a narrow stretch of shallow water known as ______ strait.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Bering'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bering Strait:**

 
 
• The Bering Strait is a narrow passage of water between Russia and Alaska.
 
• It connects the Arctic Ocean (via the Chukchi Sea) with the Pacific Ocean (via the Bering Sea).
 
• The strait is about 85 km wide at its narrowest point and is relatively shallow, with a depth of around 50 meters.
 
• It has been historically significant for human migration, as it is believed early humans crossed a land bridge here during the Ice Age.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4e94a93e26336f4c54da9e84abf46923cbefc092d9ad39fa0ba1f9ed28ceb440.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Palk Strait:**

 
 
• This strait lies between India and Sri Lanka, connecting the Bay of Bengal and the Gulf of Mannar.
 
• It has no geographical relation to the Arctic Ocean.
 
 
 
• **Hudson Strait:**
 
 
• Located in northeastern Canada, it connects Hudson Bay with the Atlantic Ocean.
 
• Though in the northern latitudes, it does not connect the Arctic and Pacific Oceans.
 
 
 
• **Bosphorus Strait:**
 
 
• This important waterway in Turkey connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Marmara, and ultimately the Mediterranean Sea.
 
• It is far from the Arctic region and plays no role in linking the Arctic Ocean with the Pacific.

questions.question: Which among the following Ministries launched the app JALDOOT?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ministry of Rural Development **has developed **“JALDOOT App”** that will be used across the country to capture the water level of selected wells in a village.
 
• **Union Minister of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj, Shri Giriraj Singh will launch the “JALDOOT App” at a function in New Delhi**.
 
• The J**aldoot app** will enable **Gram Rojgar Sahayak (GRS) **to measure the water level of selected wells twice a year (pre-monsoon and post-monsoon).
 
• In every village, adequate number of measurement locations (2-3) shall need to be selected.
 
• These will be representative of the ground water level in that village.
 
• The app will facilitate panchayats with robust data, which can be further used for better planning of works.
 
• The ground water data could be utilised as part of the **Gram Panchayat Development Plan (GPDP) and Mahatma Gandhi NREGA planning exercises**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Ministry of Finance** is a government department or ministry responsible for managing the financial affairs of a country or jurisdiction.

 
 
• Its primary role is to **develop and implement fiscal policies, manage public finances, and oversee economic matters related to taxation, budgeting, and financial regulations.**
 
 
 
• **The Ministry of Culture** is a government department or ministry that is responsible for overseeing and promoting cultural affairs within a country or jurisdiction.
 
 
• Its primary role is to** preserve, develop, and promote the cultural heritage, arts, and creative industries of a nation. **
 
 
 
• **​The Ministry of External Affairs,** also known as the **Foreign Ministry or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, is a government department or ministry responsible for a country's foreign relations and diplomacy.**
 
 
• Its primary role is to manage and conduct international relations on behalf of the country.

questions.question: Which team won the Ranji trophy 2021 - 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Madhya Pradesh** won their first Ranji Trophy**.

 
 
• 
 
**Group Stage:** Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Mumbai, Bengal, Uttarakhand, Punjab, and Uttar Pradesh won their respective groups to qualify for the quarter-finals.

 
 
• 
 
**Preliminary Quarter-Final: **Jharkhand and Nagaland won their groups. Jharkhand scored 880 runs in their first innings, which is the fourth-highest team total in Ranji Trophy history. **They extended their lead to 1008 runs, the biggest ever lead in first-class cricket, securing a place in the quarter-finals based on their first-innings lead.**

 
 
• 
 
**Quarter-Finals: **Mumbai, Uttar Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh emerged victorious in their quarter-final matches and advanced to the semi-finals.

 
 
• 
 
**Semi-Finals: **Bengal faced Jharkhand in a draw match, but Jharkhand progressed due to their first-innings lead. Madhya Pradesh defeated Bengal by 174 runs to reach their first final since the 1999 edition of the Ranji Trophy. The second semi-final between Mumbai and Uttar Pradesh was also a draw, with Mumbai advancing to the final based on their first-innings lead.

 
 
• 
 
**Final:** Madhya Pradesh faced Mumbai in the final match and won by 6 wickets, securing their first-ever Ranji Trophy title.

 
 
 
 
• Overall, Madhya Pradesh's journey in the tournament was remarkable, with notable performances in the group stage, a strong victory in the quarter-finals, and a convincing win in the final against Mumbai.
